title: Rollout telemetry runway and ordinal signal map (first-wave)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working runway doc to coordinate the first-wave rollout telemetry and 'ordinal' windows (W0..W4). Focus: capture the minimal set of probes, KPI gates, owner rotations, and quick mitigations so the team can run small-batch to broad rollouts with consistent decision points.

Notes to self / context (informal):
- 'Ordinal' = numbered rollout windows (W0 = alpha/internal, W1 = 1% external, W2 = 10%, W3 = 50%, W4 = 100%). Keeps decisioning simple for oncall and PMs.
- This is deliberately compact: telemetry + gate + action per window. Use as single source during launch ops.
- Related: RDW-4921 (traffic shaping patch) and RT-1234 (canary instrumentation).

Quick TL;DR KPI targets (currently proposed):
- p95 generation latency (end-to-end): < 220ms for small payloads, < 450ms for long (>=1024 tokens)
- error rate (5xx + model timeouts): < 0.5% rolling 5m
- latency amplification (client->platform delta): < 1.4x baseline
- cost per 1k tokens (hosted): track + alert if > baseline +20%
- prompt / hallucination signal: automated eval false-positive threshold <= 3% on sentinel prompt set

Roadmap tracker (ordinal windows):
- W0: dates: 2024-10-07..2024-10-09 | traffic: internal only | owners: Diego (eng), Aisha (prodops) | KPIs: sanity checks only (service up, basic latency) | Gate: none (alpha)
- W1: dates: 2024-10-10..2024-10-16 | traffic: 1% external | owners: Diego (eng), Claire (cs), Morgan (product) | KPIs: p95 <250ms, error <0.75% | Gate: pass 72h rolling
- W2: dates: 2024-10-17..2024-10-23 | traffic: 10% | owners: Eng SRE rotation (oncall A), ProdOps (Aisha) | KPIs: p95 <230ms, cache-hit > baseline-5%, cost within projected envelope | Gate: health 48h + manual review
- W3: dates: 2024-10-24..2024-10-30 | traffic: 50% | owners: SRE lead, Support lead | KPIs: solid SLO headroom (latency margin >=10%), incident rate trend flat or down | Gate: canary committee sign-off (slack + confluence note)
- W4: date: 2024-10-31 onward | traffic: 100% | owners: Platform ops, PM | KPIs: steady-state metrics, handoff into runbook and weekly dashboard

Signals and probes (minimal working set):
- Infra probes: node pool capacity, GPU utilization, queue/backpressure depth, request queue length
- Latency probes: p50/p95/p99 by model, by route; tail recursion for streaming endpoints
- Cost probes: estimated tokens processed per minute, projected burn for 24h window
- Quality probes: sentinel prompt-set eval (10 prompts) — automated scoring every 30m; human-sample batch every 6h
- Behavioral probes: rate of tool/function calls failing, malformed JSON outputs, hallucination markers

Gate decision rubric (example for W1 -> W2):
- Green: all KPIs within targets for 72h, no more than 1 customer-facing incident, ops runbook validated -> proceed
- Yellow: a single KPI outside target but trending stable and mitigation exists (scaling, fallback model) -> extend W1 for +48h and re-evaluate
- Red: >1 KPI outside target or any incident that materially affects user experience -> rollback to previous window or enable emergency fallback routing (dedicated small model pool)

Owner rotor & playbook (short):
- Daily: prodops p.m. (Aisha) posts ETA + short signal summary in #prodops-rollouts at 09:00 PT
- Oncall (SRE): monitors infra probes, makes scaling calls; escalation -> eng lead + PM at threshold breaches
- Support: triage customer tickets, classify as ops/quality, forward to Claire + eng owning model
- Deploy owner (Diego): coordinate canary ramps and handle rollback script (automated safe rollback in pipeline)

Checklist (pre-window for each ordinal):
- [ ] Canary config validated in staging with same traffic shaping rules
- [ ] Instrumentation (tracing, logs, metric tags) present for all routes in rollout group
- [ ] Alert burnbook created (escalations + runbook links)
- [ ] Capacity cushion verified (min spare GPUs = 15% above expected peak)
- [ ] Cost throttle policy set (stop ramp if projected 24h cost > budget threshold)
- [ ] Sentinel prompt set uploaded and baseline scores recorded

Escapes and fallbacks (fast moves):
- Immediate: enable fallback model variant (lower-memory / quantized) in routing policy if p95 > 600ms or error spike >2%
- Short-term: pause ramp and redirect 100% of new traffic to dedicated pool in us-west
- Longer-term: full rollback to previous release + postmortem + hotfix release plan

Telemetry dashboard sketch (fields to include):
- window_id, traffic_pct, p50, p95, p99, error_rate_5m, cache_hit_rate, est_cost_24h, sentinel_score, owner_oncall, notes
- (example row) W1 | 1% | 110ms | 180ms | 310ms | 0.12% | 63% | $18/day est | 91% | Diego: no issues

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final thresholds for cost alerts (Aisha to propose by 2024-10-04).
- Confirm whether model-variant fallback preserves user-level state (session continuity) — eng to confirm (Diego).
- Add automated ticket creation for sentinel_score drop below 85% (integrate with PagerDuty or linear).

Appendix: quick jump commands (ops cheats):
- rollback: ./scripts/rollback-to-tag.sh --tag stable-2024-10-01 --force
- trigger sentinel eval: ./tools/sentinel-run --env prod --prompts sentinels.json
- scale up pool: infra scale-gpu-pool --region us-west --add 4

Slack anchors / references:
- #prodops-rollouts (live ops chatter)
- thread: C1a9f (canary instrumentation questions)
- confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RT-1234 (canary instrumentation design)

Notes / style: keep this doc intentionally short. Use it as the single-pane checklist + telemetry reference during the launch window. Move final decision notes into the canary committee's confluence page after each window completes.

Last edited by Morgan Lin — draft: will iterate with Aisha and Diego after the next run-through on 2024-10-04.
